title: Phase 78 eo (effectively-once) fault-matrix — deployed Shuffle / IRIS

deployed_shuffle_test.note: All executions issued through the deployed Shuffle workflow c6b3fcd8-13e5-44a8-a818-024e4ae4422b execute_python node; not a host-side substitute.

stable_source_id.note: Same stable id across two executions -> same IRIS object (DUP_SKIP, cached alert_id); marker parity confirmed.

create_only.note: Deterministic doc id claim returns 409 on 2nd claim; no overwrite. op_type=create guarantees single object.

occ.note: Optimistic-concurrency / create-only protects the ledger; replay claim 409, no mutation.

delivered_immutable.note: DELIVERED record is never mutated; replay returns DUP_SKIP with same alert_id, blocking automated retry.

partial_success.note: IRIS accepted then ledger/dedup-write failed -> RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED; exactly 1 IRIS object, no duplicate.

crash_after_accept.note: After IRIS POST (object created), simulated crash before ledger finalize; dedup left RECONCILE_CRASH; replay blocked, no 2nd object.

response_loss.note: Simulated lost response after IRIS accept; alert_id not recorded; exactly 1 IRIS object, replay blocked.

timeout_ambiguity.note: Ambiguous timeout -> RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED (object created, ledger left in reconcile); no 2nd object.

reconciliation_blocks_replay.note: After RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED, replay returns RECONCILE_PENDING (fail-closed, no_duplicate); automated replay blocked.

race_campaign.note: 10 concurrent identical executions -> exactly 1 IRIS object; 9 DUP_SKIP/RECONCILE_PENDING, 1 ROUTED.

direct_readback.note: Confirmed via IRIS REST API GET (200) with marker parity, not a substitute.

fault_window_single_identity.note: Entire fault window on one identity yielded exactly ONE IRIS object (625); all faults/replays blocked from creating a second.

method_notes: Dedup credentials are supplied to the deployed execute_python node from the dedicated secret dedup-shuffle-dedicated (mounted into the execution sandbox; read by the v2 code via load_env/os.environ). The published OpenSearch 9200 is firewalled from the execution sandbox, so the test variant connects via the cert-valid hostname 'shuffle-opensearch' while resolving it to the reachable container IP 172.20.0.3 (TLS verification preserved). This is fully reversible: only the node 'code' was changed; the original v2 code is restored after the matrix and no node environment credentials remain.
cleanup: Synthetic dedup rows deleted by id; IRIS alerts left isolated (no DB delete).
